text:
maya: Quick sync — I sketched a lightweight decision doc for chat streaming semantics. Need to lock SSE vs WS, delta envelope format, and finish-reason behavior before next week's alpha. TL;DR: customers want lower latency + predictable partial outputs for streaming UIs.

samir: can you paste the doc link?

maya: https://redwood.internal/notes/streaming-semantics-draft (draft) — highlights below.

jess: biggest pragmatic constraint is mobile proxies and corporate firewalls — some customers reported SSE being blocked in older proxies. WS tends to work more reliably through proxies but is slightly more complex server-side.

ellie: +1 on that. Also: iOS backgrounding kills SSE streams more often. WS reconnect semantics are nicer for our SDKs.

maya: Agreed. But SSE has simpler server model and lower footprint for hosted API (no per-connection state beyond cursors). We need to weigh cost/perf delta.

ana: From product/customer asks: two asks stood out — 1) streaming partial tokens for realtime chat UIs, 2) deterministic finish reasons (e.g., \"stop_token\", \"max_tokens\", \"user_cancel\") that clients can rely on for UX and billing. Customers want a canonical migration path.

samir: technical tradeoffs I see:
```
- SSE: server -> client event stream, simple reconnect, payloads are text/event-stream
- WS: bidirectional, binary frames possible, lower latency for many small messages, easier to multiplex tool calls
```

samir: Also we need to decide delta format: per-token events (one event per token) vs chunked-deltas (multi-token payloads). Per-token is great for live typing UX but increases overhead/requests. Chunked is better for throughput and reduces SSE/WS frame pressure.

jess: For launch MVP we should default to chunked-deltas with a small max chunk size (eg 64 tokens) and opt-in per-token mode for SDKs that request it. That gives good compromise.

ellie: Agree. Add a server-configurable batching window (e.g., 30–100ms) so latency/throughput tunable per-customer.

maya: Proposed finish-reason schema (canonical strings): 
```
- "stop": normal completion (model emitted stop tokens)
- "max_tokens": reached max tokens
- "cancelled": client requested cancel/close
- "error": server-side error
- "fallback": server fell back to cheaper/compatible model
```

maya: Important: clients must treat stream termination + final metadata message as authoritative. We should emit a final JSON "done" event with `finish_reason` and stats (tokens, latency, model_id).

ana: Launch criteria checklist suggestion: 
- Docs + SDK examples for SSE and WS (one page each)
- Default semantics implemented in hosted API + Redwood SDKs
- Canary with 5 customers (mix of mobile/web) running for 2 weeks
- Observability: per-request token counts, stream disconnect rate, average chunk size
- Fallthrough policy: automatic fallback to polling if streaming fails 3x in a row per-client

jess: I want a small compatibility contract: if client requests `streaming: true` with `format: token` and server doesn't support per-token it should return `streaming: supported: false` with `recommended: chunked` and 409-ish semantics. Keep it explicit.

samir: Ops note: WS requires sticky routing for connection affinity if we keep per-connection KV cache. For SSE/polling we can be more stateless. That affects Dedicated/Private customers who pin models.

ellie: UX ask: editor integrations want partial structured JSON outputs for incremental rendering (not just plain text). We need a small extension to the delta envelope to carry `structured_chunk` with `content_type`. Example: 
```json
{ "delta": {"type":"structured_chunk","content_type":"application/json+schema.v1","payload":"{...}"} }
```

maya: We should include structured payload support but keep it opt-in and gated behind `accepts_structured=true` in the request. Avoid breaking existing clients.

ana: Prioritization: Customers pushing structured streaming are two enterprise accounts (legal search + analytics). Recommend we put structured streaming in next quarter's roadmap after we ship core streaming.

jess: For the API: keep a single endpoint /v1/chat/streams, with `transport: sse|ws|none`, `delta_format: chunked|token`, `accepts_structured: boolean`. Keep defaults: transport=ws, delta_format=chunked, accepts_structured=false. Document expected events and final `done` event.

maya: Deployment plan: 1) internal SDKs + server impl, 2) hosted canary w/ 5 customers, 3) public docs + examples, 4) flag rollout and metrics.

samir: One more constraint: mobile SDKs should expose auto-reconnect with exponential backoff + resume semantics when using WS and server must allow a resume token to avoid re-generation when resuming within short window.

ellie: Will the resume token be persisted server-side or encoded? Prefer stateless signed resume tokens that encode last-kv-cursor to allow resume without sticky routing. Security review needed.

maya: OK. Action items:
- samir: prototype WS sticky vs signed-resume comparison (perf + infra cost) — due EOD Thu
- jess: write MVP delta envelope spec and SDK examples (chunked + per-token opt-in) — due Mon
- ellie: validate mobile backgrounding behavior and add reconnection guidance — due Mon
- ana: line up 3-5 canary customers and confirm acceptance criteria — due next Wed

ops-bot: Deployed: `feature/streaming-mvp` to staging at 2026-03-19T18:12Z :rocket:

maya: Thanks all — will sync Fri 11am to finalize launch gates. If we choose WS default we should call it out explicitly in the docs and include migration notes for SSE-first customers.

samir: +1. Also add a small benchmark table for token/second throughput for SSE vs WS in the doc.

jess: i'll add perf numbers to the spec PR.

ellie: tagging @platform-team for resume-token security review next week.

maya: End thread — feel free to add short replies if you have objections.
